headline: Contributors get readable game structures and safer refactoring tools
summary: Contributors can navigate source by game system and use named levels, buttons, hero states and shared structures instead of many raw numbers and private copies. The refactoring preserves the original compiled bytes: all 5,116 functions and all 3,713,096 code bytes in the snapshot remain matched, meaning they compile to the same bytes as the original game. Data moved into C now builds from values generated from each contributor's own disc, with 516,916 of 699,072 data bytes matched in the final snapshot.
highlights: Source-moving and full-match checking tools support nested folders; CI checks syntax, tool tests, lint and progress, while matching still needs local checks with a disc and toolchain (#166, #168, #170).
Shared headers and named fields replace duplicated hero, controller, camera, collision and object views; views that would change bytes remain private (#172, #174, #175, #177, #183).
Suspect compiler tricks are catalogued; unnecessary ones were removed, and required cases retain explanations (#194, #195, #201, #202).
Generated data declarations cover ordinary values and pointer blocks without committing retail values (#196, #197, #198).
The level extraction issue #165 was closed as completed.
